newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia diamond monopoly ups output, sees increase.
newsitem.headline: Russia diamond monopoly ups output, sees increase.

text.p: Russia's biggest diamond producer Almazy Rossii-Sakha raised production of rough stones by three percent in 1996 compared to the previous year's level, a senior company official said at the weekend.
Last year the company mined $1.38 billion worth of rough stones.
Almazy president Vyacheslav Shtyrov said the company planned to boost output by 25 percent in the coming three years with the help of foreign funding.
Shtyrov said Almazy still planned to draw a $500 million loan from foreign banks through NatWest Markets.
NatWest has postponed the loan agreement with Almazy until the Russian government and South African diamond group De Beers can conclude talks on an expired diamond marketing agreement.
But Shtyrov said that there was no direct link between the loan and the agreement with De Beers. If the agreement is not reached, the company will look for other investments, he said.
Under a memorandum of understanding between Russia and De Beers, Almazy has been named the sole authorised exporter of Russian rough diamonds.
Shtyrov said the Russian government could aprrove the long-delayed deal later this month.
De Beers stopped purchasing diamonds from Russia on December 31 last year when it cancelled an interim arrangement after the Russian side failed to approve or reject a new trade deal.
